Build an intervention object from efficacy parameters

Source: R/interventions.R
build_intervention.Rd

Constructs an intervention effects object from user-supplied initial efficacy values (deterrency, pre-prandial killing, post-prandial killing) and a parametric attrition decay function. The three columns of each effects matrix correspond to: (1) protected humans, (2) unprotected humans, (3) animals.

Two model structures are supported and are mutually exclusive:

  • Standard (3-host): uses Deterrency, PrePrandial, and PostPrandial.

  • Dummy-host (4-host): uses Deterrency, KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute, and PostPrandial. A fourth dummy-host column is added to all effects matrices. Do not supply PrePrandial together with KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute.

Usage

build_intervention(
  efficacy,
  halflife_attrition = NULL,
  shape_attrition = NULL,
  decay_attrition = "weibull",
  duration_years = 3,
  model_p = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  halflife_insecticide = NULL,
  component_decay = NULL,
  insecticide_decay = TRUE
)

Arguments

efficacy

Non-empty numeric vector with unique component names and finite, non-missing values, using any subset of the following efficacy parameters:

  • "Deterrency" in [0,1] — reduces host availability (alphai) for protected humans; deterred mosquitoes keep searching.

  • "PrePrandial" in [0,1] — pre-prandial killing: reduces the probability that a mosquito that has found a protected human bites and survives (PBi); mosquitoes failing this stage die. Standard model only.

  • "PostPrandial" in [0,1] — post-prandial killing: reduces the probability of surviving after feeding on a protected human to find a resting place (PCi).

  • "KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute" \(\geq 0\) — killing during host-seeking via a dummy-host mechanism. Dummy-host model only. An absolute rate, not a probability: it is used directly as the availability of the dummy host (one per protected person), in the same units as the host availabilities alphai. Values from experimental hut fits that are relative to the control availability alpha_0 (KillingDuringHostSeekingRelative) must first be multiplied by alpha_0 (get_ITN_params() does this).

Note on time units: the experimental hut model has no time scale (its rates are per hut-night), whereas the rates of this package are per day, with td the duration of host seeking. By convention, a hut-night is treated as a day: KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute is used directly as a per-day rate, without dividing by td. This is provisional, until the experimental hut fitting model is improved. With this convention, the field impacts of the dummy-host parameterisations are of the same order as those of the standard parameterisations of the same trials, whereas dividing by td gives systematically higher impacts (the standard model is not a validated benchmark either).

halflife_attrition

Attrition decay parameter L (days): the half-life for Weibull / exponential / Hill, the time to zero for linear / step / smooth-compact (see decay_function()).

shape_attrition

Shape parameter kappa of the attrition decay function (for Weibull / Hill / smooth-compact; set to NULL otherwise).

decay_attrition

Attrition decay function: "weibull", "exponential", "hill", "linear", "step", "smooth-compact" or "none" (see decay_function()). Default "weibull".

duration_years

Single finite positive duration in years. One interpolation point per day is used, with at least one point: npoints = max(round(365 * duration_years), 1). Default 3 years.

model_p

Model object from build_model_obj().

name

Optional label for the intervention.

mode

Optional character; "standard" or "dummy_host". When supplied, overrides auto-detection from the names of efficacy. The object returned by get_ITN_params() includes a mode field that can be passed here directly.

halflife_insecticide

Optional named numeric vector (years), using the same names as efficacy, triggering an additional per-component linear insecticide decay on top of the main attrition: the efficacy of a component is multiplied by \(1 - t / (365 \cdot hl)\). Despite its name, \(hl\) is the time at which the effect reaches zero (the effect halves at \(hl / 2\)). This is the convention of the Champagne et al. (2025) parameterisations returned by get_ITN_params(), where \(hl = a / (1 - Washed / Unwashed)\), with \(a\) the aging time of the trial's washed arm (3 years, 2 for Sovegnon), so that efficacy after \(a\) years equals the washed (20x) value. Negative values (washed efficacy higher than unwashed) make the effect increase linearly over time; Inf means no insecticide decay. Zero and NaN values are invalid; NA means unspecified. For other decay shapes, use component_decay.

component_decay

Optional named list specifying an independent decay function for each efficacy component, using the same names as efficacy. Each element is a list with fields decay (string), L (days; meaning depends on the shape, see decay_function()), and optionally kappa. An explicit shape always overrides halflife_insecticide for the same component. Constant shapes ("none", "constant") need no L or kappa; other shapes require a positive L and, where applicable, a positive kappa. Incomplete specifications raise an error instead of falling back to linear or constant decay.

insecticide_decay

Logical (default TRUE). If FALSE, halflife_insecticide and component_decay are ignored: the efficacies keep their initial (e.g. unwashed) values throughout and only attrition decays. If TRUE, the per-component insecticide decay is applied and, in addition, a Weibull decay is fitted for each efficacy component to the product attrition \(\times\) insecticide decay (see Value).

Value

A list of length 1 containing the intervention specification, ready to pass to calculate_impact(). Standard model: 3-column effects matrices. Dummy-host model: 4-column effects matrices. When insecticide_decay = TRUE, the element fitted_decay is a data frame with one row per efficacy component and columns component, L (Weibull half-life, days), kappa and rmse: the single Weibull per component (starting at 1) that best approximates attrition \(\times\) insecticide decay over the intervention duration (as used for OpenMalaria GVI parameterisations). The model itself always uses the exact (unfitted) decay. The element settings keeps the inputs (efficacy, mode, attrition and per-component decays, insecticide_decay), used by get_OM_GVI_snippet(). The element param_set is the same intervention as a one-row param_sets table of run_interventions(), which calculate_impact() evaluates. Several interventions are combined with c().
